$comment: Defect ledger for the adversarial extractor corpus (#702).
test/fixtures/ is happy-path only: 36 fixtures, 36 pass, while ten languages
corrupt, truncate or drop declarations on inputs that appear in ordinary code.
A green suite that misses that is worse than no suite, because it is the
evidence cited for the tier labels in KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md.
test/expected-adversarial/ snapshots what each extractor ACTUALLY produces
today. This file records which of those snapshot lines are WRONG, what the
correct signature would be, and which issue owns the fix. So:
- a behaviour change with no ledger update fails (regression caught)
- a FIX also fails, because the snapshot no longer matches (forces the
ledger entry to be removed, so the ledger cannot rot)
- `defects: 0` for a language is a positive claim that it handles the
adversarial cases, not an absence of testing
`shouldBe` is the signature a correct extractor would emit. It is prose-exact
where that is unambiguous and indicative where the rendering is a choice.

defects.note: The keyword-only `*` marker is dropped, so a caller cannot tell `b` is keyword-only. Defaults collapsing to `...` is deliberate normalisation, not a defect. The Tier-2 regex fallback drops this declaration entirely — only the AST tier reaches it at all.
Same first-`)` truncation as Kotlin; `2` becomes a phantom parameter.

defects.actual: func closureParam(cb) → Int, n: Int) -> Int  :6-6
defects.note: Structurally malformed: the arrow substitution fires inside the closure type, then the remainder of the real parameter list is appended as prose. The worst single output in the corpus.
Renders correctly by luck — `[String: [Int]]` carries no parentheses — but shares the unmigrated scanner, so it is listed to keep the language's status honest.
First-`)` truncation; phantom `2`; return type lost.
`)` inside the string default truncates; return type lost.

defects.shouldBe: case class Dto  :15-15  followed by  class Consumer  :17-21  with `consume` attributed to Consumer
defects.note: `(?:[^{]*)\{` on the class header matches newlines, so a body-less `case class` walks past the blank line into the next declaration and adopts its body: Dto is anchored :15-21 (Consumer's span), carries Consumer's `consume`, and **class Consumer is never reported**. Misattribution rather than truncation — every symbol named is real, just bolted to the wrong owner. Kotlin had the identical defect and its scanner migration fixed it; Scala awaits its own increment.

defects.actual: namedParams(int a, {int b = 2, int Function(int) → int  :3-3
defects.shouldBe: namedParams(int a, {int b, int Function(int)? cb}) → int
defects.note: The `Function(int)` parameter type opens a paren the scanner never closes; the brace group is left unterminated and the return type is spliced onto the fragment.
`)` inside the string default ends the scan mid-literal, emitting an unterminated quote.

defects.actual: pub fn closure_param(a: i32, b: Box<dyn Fn(i32) → i32>) -> i32  :2-4
defects.shouldBe: pub fn closure_param(a: i32, b: Box<dyn Fn(i32) -> i32>) → i32
defects.note: The `->` to `→` substitution hits the FIRST arrow, which belongs to the closure type, leaving the real return arrow as literal `-> i32`. Params survive; the rendering states the return type twice in two notations.

defects.actual: pub fn deep_generics(v: Vec<Box<dyn Fn(i32) → i32>>) -> usize  :5-7
defects.shouldBe: pub fn deep_generics(v: Vec<Box<dyn Fn(i32) -> i32>>) → usize

defects.shouldBe: NestedDefault(int a, int b = G(1, 2)) → int
defects.note: Loses the closing paren of the parameter list — visibly unbalanced, so at least a reader can tell it is damaged.
Truncates at the nested `)`; the second parameter is lost.
